description: Measures where the c_3 anchor-dependence lives. The h*D carrier is anchor-blind (3.53e-7) while S varies by 1.245, so the bridge carries ~3.5e6 times more variation -- essentially all of it -- and changes sign between anchors. B is a defined quotient, not a derived decomposition; two anchors cannot constrain its form and none is proposed.

data.verdict: LOCALISED (scope-(a) measurement). The anchor-dependence of c_3 lives ENTIRELY in the h*D -> S bridge: the carrier varies by 3.529e-7 between anchors while S varies by 1.245, a factor of 3.52902e+6. The bridge B := S/(h*D) is +11.319 at the proton anchor and -2.778 at the muon anchor -- it CHANGES SIGN, so 'S = h*D up to a factor' understates the gap and no positive rescaling of the carrier reaches S at both anchors. B is a QUOTIENT DEFINED HERE, not a derived decomposition: with exactly two anchors, any 2-parameter family fits it exactly, so its FORM is not constrained by this data and none is proposed. The contribution is negative-shaped and about direction: routes that hope to explain the anchor-dependence from the ladder are looking where the signal provably is not. No value derived, no c_k wired, no fit; nothing bears on q0 (forever-gated, qou-eic1).

q0AnchorReason: Deliberately BOTH pins: this probe compares the proton-anchored and muon-anchored evaluations against each other, so it is a cross-anchor measurement rather than a single-layer compute. Recorded as ambiguous rather than picking one, since picking one would misdescribe what is measured. Both values are read from the committed k=31 re-pin witness; no modulus is computed here.
